design.name: 毕方
design.brief: The bifang (毕方) of the Shan Hai Jing, 'shaped like a crane, with ONE SINGLE LEG, red markings on a dark ground and a white beak', whose appearance brings strange fires: a tall slender crane-like bird about 2 m tall standing on EXACTLY ONE long thin leg placed in the middle under its body, ending in one foot with three forward toes and one back toe; it has NO second leg anywhere, not even tucked up. A long S-curved neck, a long sharp white beak holding a glowing coal ember (衔火) that glows yellow-orange (weak spot), a crest of a few stiff vermilion flame-shaped feathers, deep blue-black plumage boldly patterned with vermilion stripes and spots, wings folded tightly against the body with flame-shaped vermilion tips, a short fan of stiff tail feathers. Elegant, eerie and sharp-eyed; it perches high on pillars and spears fire with its beak.
design.style_note: Stylization: cartoon game proportions in the same family as the desert and frost rosters (jerboa soldier, fire rat, sancai tomb beast, golden snub-nosed monkey): chunky simplified masses, oversized heads and hands or paws, toy-like readable forms with clean bevelled edges. Iron, basalt and bronze as a few big faceted plates with sparse painted wear; lava and fire painted as OPAQUE glowing cracks, seams and solid sculpted flame shapes (never transparent fire, smoke or particles); fur, hair and feathers as a few large carved clumps. Feathers are big simple carved shapes. Count the legs: in EVERY view there is exactly ONE leg under the body. Its wings stay folded or half-raised for balance, never spread like a hovering bird.
design.turnaround_pose: standing upright on its ONE single leg (exactly one leg in every view, straight and centred under the body, no second leg, nothing tucked up), wings folded tightly against the body, the long neck in a relaxed S-curve, head level facing straight ahead, beak closed holding the ember painted as opaque bright yellow-orange (no flame, no halo), crest feathers up, the short tail fan pointing straight back
design.turnaround_digits: the single foot with three forward toes and one back toe, clearly countable; the crest, beak tip and tail fully inside the frame.
